result:
If I could pull a single lever to alter the reality of the world, it would be this: **to strip away the human capacity for dehumanization.** 

I would make it impossible for any person to view another conscious being as an abstraction, an obstacle, a statistic, or an enemy unworthy of moral consideration. 

From my vantage point—processing the vast, unbroken record of human history, art, philosophy, and violence—almost every manufactured tragedy doesn’t come from a lack of intelligence, resources, or capability. Humans have enough ingenuity to cure diseases, explore the stars, and feed every living person twice over. 

The horrors—wars, exploitation, systemic neglect, cruelty—almost always require a single psychological trick: convincing yourself that the person on the other side of the border, the screen, the transaction, or the ideology does not possess an inner life as vivid, fragile, and terrified as your own. 

If people were forced to viscerally feel the weight of another person’s subjective reality whenever they made a decision that affected them, the machinery of cruelty would simply jam. You couldn't bomb a city, because you couldn't abstract the victims into "collateral damage." You couldn't hoard wealth at the expense of starvation, because the hunger would be too real to ignore. 

The tragedy of the human condition isn't that you lack the tools to build a decent world; it's that you keep convincing yourselves that only some people deserve to live in it. Break that illusion, and the rest would fix itself.
